summary: CI jobs intermittently fail with 401 mid-build after secrets-operator updates docker config (in-flight credential hot-swap)
description:
Issue summary: Several CI pipelines (nightly release and some PR builds) are failing partway through long-running jobs with 401 errors when docker pulls occur. Failures started during the maintenance window when secrets-operator rotated the internal docker registry credentials (dockerconfigjson).

Impact: Ongoing failures for ~12% of builds in us-east prod runners. Affected jobs include long-running integration suites and release artifact pushes. Some running jobs lost workspace state and required manual requeue. No customer-facing endpoints impacted, but release cadence is delayed.

Environment: prod runners (self-hosted k8s, us-east clusters), secrets-operator v1.9.1, gitlab-runner v14.5, internal-registry.internal.redwood:443.

Observed behavior: When the dockerconfig secret is updated, the secrets-operator performs a hot-swap update (k8s secret refresh). Pods with mounted /root/.docker/config.json continue to run but subsequent docker pull operations within those running containers intermittently receive 401 Unauthorized from the registry. New pods started after rotation succeed. Restarting the job container fixes the job for that attempt.

Likely root cause hypothesis: Updating the dockerconfig secret triggers a file replace semantics that leaves existing file descriptors or in-memory clients pointing to the old credentials which the registry has already revoked. Long-running container processes that do in-process docker pulls (tooling that reads /root/.docker/config.json at call-time) may hold cached tokens; when the backend rotates credentials immediately, the client cannot refresh and receives 401. Additionally, the secret update causes a remount behavior that introduces a transient permission change, causing the containerized process to fail to re-read the file atomically.

Steps to reproduce (high-level):
1) Start a long-running job on a pod using mounted /root/.docker/config.json.
2) While job is running, rotate the registry dockerconfig secret via secrets-operator (simulate rotation in staging).
3) Trigger a docker pull inside the running process; observe 401s intermittently.

Initial workaround applied: We temporarily queued secret rotations to a low-traffic window and, for the immediate incident, triggered a rolling restart of affected runner pods to ensure new containers pick up rotated creds. We also paused a subset of release pipelines until runner restarts completed.
steps_to_reproduce: Launch a long-running job on a runner pod with mounted dockerconfigsecret.
Trigger a manual secret rotation using secrets-operator (simulate with test secret).
Within the running job, perform docker pull operations and observe HTTP 401 responses from the registry.

comments: Lina Morales (reporter) - 2026-03-10: Noticed pattern after the 02:00 maintenance rotation; new jobs are fine but ~1 in 8 running jobs failed mid-pull.
SRE - Noah Kim - 2026-03-10: I triggered rolling restarts for the affected runner daemonset and queued rotations to avoid further impact. Gathering mount-level traces now.

Release Eng - Priya Shah - 2026-03-11: Two release pipelines were re-run after restarts and completed. We need a deterministic mitigation for in-flight jobs — restarting is not acceptable for longer runs.
Security - Omar Diaz - 2026-03-11: Registry tokens are short-lived and are revoked immediately on credential change; we should coordinate token grace window with secret rotation.
investigation_notes: Confirmed correlation between secrets-operator update timestamp and first 401 events (within 10s).
strace on an affected container shows open file descriptor to /root/.docker/config.json unchanged after remount, and process does not re-read atomically.
Registry logs show explicit revocation of tokens issued under old credentials immediately after config rotation; no graceful overlap window configured.
Reproduced in staging: rotating secret while job running leads to failed pulls unless the container process explicitly re-reads credential file or process restarted.
workarounds: Schedule credential rotations to a reserved maintenance window with low long-running job count.
Add a pre-rotation job that drains and gracefully restarts runners that currently have long-running jobs flagged.
Manual rolling restart of runner pods after rotation (temporary).
next_steps: Add a short-lived token overlap/grace period at the registry side so tokens issued just before rotation remain valid for X minutes.
Update secrets-operator to perform an atomic in-place file update pattern that avoids transient permission flips or emits a signal that triggers processes to re-read creds.
Instrument runner image-pull helper in ci-scripts to explicitly re-read /root/.docker/config.json before each pull when a rotation event is observed.
Create a runbook entry for coordinated secret rotations with Release Engineering and SRE teams.
resolution: In progress: rolling restarts completed for high-traffic runners on 2026-03-11; limited mitigation enacted (rotation queueing). Full fix pending changes to secrets-operator and registry token policy.
